findings.description: The bucket declares no ACL restriction and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and is explicitly annotated as public, so objects it holds (including the uploaded customer master file) can be read by anonymous internet users.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so customer data objects are stored without enforced server-side encryption (no SSE-KMS).
No logging block is configured, so access to this publicly reachable bucket leaves no audit trail, preventing detection or investigation of unauthorized data access.

Object versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects in a publicly writable bucket can be overwritten or destroyed irreversibly, enabling data tampering or destruction without recovery.

A 'customer-master.xlsx' file, presumably containing sensitive customer records, is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly accessible aws_s3_bucket.data with no kms_key_id or server-side encryption specified, exposing PII to anonymous download.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, leaving its contents unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to financial data is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so the private ACL is the only barrier; a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly with no account/bucket-level guard.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so financial records can be irreversibly overwritten or deleted by anyone with write access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data in the operations bucket is stored without server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of object-level access to this bucket.
The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so public ACLs or bucket policies could later be applied without being blocked at the bucket boundary.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest despite versioning and logging being configured.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, leaving it one ACL or policy change away from public exposure.

The central log bucket relies solely on the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so an ACL or policy change could expose collected access logs, which contain sensitive operational detail.
force_destroy is true on the bucket that aggregates access logs for other buckets, allowing the audit trail to be deleted wholesale in a single operation and undermining forensic integrity.
